In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the independence of irrelevant-alternatives condition of Pattanaig and Peleg [8] is necessary for the existence of a strategy proof social choice function.
the question: What is the weakest condition one can impose on decision schemes to obtain random dictatorships?
the question of when a social decision scheme is a random dictatorship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the random dictatorship result is a consequence of strategy proofness and regularity.
a decision super-scheme is a random dictatorship if and only if it satisfies the strategy-proofness condition and the condition of regularity.

the following conditions are equivalent: (a) the decision super-scheme is strategy-proof, (b) the decision super- scheme is regular and rationalizable and (c) the decision super scheme is a random dictatorship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, when there is a continuum of alternatives and a continuum of individuals, rationality and strategy proofness together with a condition that there be at most two individuals who have a preference over all others in the society can characterize random dictatorships.

the rationalizability requirement in McLennan [6] can be replaced by regularity and that the independence of irrelevant alternates condition and the requirement that there be more alternatives than there are individuals can be replaced by monotonicity.

, in a society with at least three alternatives, if there are more than two individuals, the independence of the irrelevant alternatives condition can be replaced by a weaker condition to obtain an alternative characterizations of random dictatorships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the random dictatorship result can be obtained without any assumption about the rationalizability of the decision super-scheme.
, in some cases, the rationalizability condition can be replaced by a weaker condition.
, when the universal set has at least three alternatives, the random dictatorships are the unique social choice functions that are both strategy proof and regular.
